claims.text: Controlled pre-annealing induces a continuous Cu-rich intergranular network in FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
Controlled pre-annealing induces a thin protective chromia scale on FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
The combined Cu-rich network and chromia scale improve high-temperature wear resistance relative to the as-deposited coating.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a fine-grained microstructure.
A 500°C, 1-hour pre-anneal in a controlled low-oxygen atmosphere is the proposed intervention.
The hypothesized wear-resistance mechanism applies at approximately 600°C and contact pressures of 0.5–2 GPa under limited oxidation.
Pre-annealing causes thermally activated copper diffusion and segregation along grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary Cu-rich phase is lubricious and reduces friction during sliding.
Controlled limited oxidation forms a thin Cr-rich chromia scale.
The chromia scale is stable and passivates the coating surface.
The Cu-rich network and chromia scale minimize localized deformation during high-temperature sliding.
The Cu-rich network and chromia scale suppress crack initiation during high-temperature sliding.
Reduced localized deformation and crack initiation lower overall wear.
At 600°C, the pre-annealed coating will have a lower coefficient of friction than the as-deposited coating.
At 600°C, the pre-annealed coating will have a lower wear rate than the as-deposited coating.
Post-test microscopy will reveal a continuous Cu-rich phase along grain boundaries.
Post-test microscopy will reveal a detectable thin chromia scale.
The pre-annealed coating will exhibit fewer wear-related damage features than the as-deposited coating.
Excessive grain growth or copper over-segregation could occur during pre-annealing.
